verdicts.section: API: k_block_tokens<geometry>() = 16 for a VNNI slot, 0 for row-major (PR3' 2a)
verdicts.concern: A size with a sentinel value (0 = 'no block save') is the pattern Ben called a smell when it was a named bool (C7: 'make the arguments proper enums'); here it is worse because 0 is a legal-looking token count. The values already exist: k_vnni::layout_on<N> and k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16. The question model.hpp really asks is 'does this slot save K in blocks', a bool. The Ben-shaped alternative is to remove the question from model.hpp altogether: set_k_block handles a row-major slot too (16 set_k_row calls inside the cache), so store_k_block has one path. That changes which thread stores row-major K (helpers would then store it too), so bytes are the same but the OFF build's thread assignment and its TTFT are not; it needs a measurement before it can be called behaviour-preserving.
verdicts.change: Minimal: `template <kv_geometry geometry> static constexpr bool k_saves_in_blocks()` (or a page-level constexpr bool) and use k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16 for the size where it is true. Record the one-path alternative as an open item with the measurement that would decide it (OFF build, llama-3.1-8b prompt 8192 TTFT, base vs one-path).

verdicts.section: API: set_k_block overloads (PR3' 2c: std::array<Row, 16> of row views + present; PR4' 2f: no present)
verdicts.concern: Two problems. (1) The stack adds a `present` mask in PR3' and removes it in PR4'; Ben asks why a shape exists when the next change deletes it. The bytes do not need it: a partial last block stored per row through Ben's set_k_row(expr) writes the same values as the masked store_block, and the absent rows are not written in either form; only the store instruction sequence of at most one block per sequence per pass differs. (2) An std::array of 16 view objects is a representation detail (C5). The 16 activation rows of one kv_head are a strided 2-D region of the per-token tensors; tron's view type carries a stride (the `view<bf16, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, VIEW_DMA_FALSE, seq<head_size>, sseq<1>>` pattern Ben deduplicated in #4697, C12), so one `view<X, ..., seq<16, head_size>, sseq<stride, 1>>` argument may cover it. Existing operation: tensor/k_vnni.hpp store_block (typed masked 16-token store) for the VNNI side; Ben's set_k_row(expr) for the row-major side.
verdicts.change: Give PR3' the final signature (no `present`): a full block goes through store_block, a partial last block through set_k_row(expr) per present row inside the same page function. Check whether the activation rows for one block and one kv_head form one strided view; if so take that view instead of std::array<Row, 16>. State the partial-block instruction change in the PR3' body as a non-byte difference.

verdicts.section: API: k_store_window_t operations open / enter / claim / finish / join (PR3' 2d)
verdicts.concern: Making the protocol a type with named operations is what Ben asked for in C3 and C12 (two control flows in save_k_impl -> helpers; a subtle pattern repeated -> one place). But tron already has the primitive the design hand-rolls: latch_ref (h/tron/threading.hpp:110-170) offers wait_until_geq (enter and join), operator++ and count_down (finish), reset (open), mwaitx-based waiting instead of a pause loop, and a watchdog driven by TRON_LATCH_WATCHDOG. Ben's C4 ('why not mask_t') and C2 (an undocumented env var or a private timeout constant, k_join_timeout_s = 120 s) both apply: he will ask why the window does not use latch_ref. Caveats: latch_trigger objects normally come from a latch_arena (make_latch), the window lives in batch (common.hpp), and latch_ref uses acq_rel on count_down where the window uses release on finished.fetch_add, so the section 4 rule 'memory orders unchanged' and the reuse pull in opposite directions.
verdicts.change: Decide before PR3': either keep the hand-rolled type and answer the latch_ref question in the PR body (why: the window must live in batch without an arena, and the join needs the unit-claim counter in the abort message), or build the type on latch_ref and state the acq_rel-for-release change as a deliberate strengthening. The claim() operation (fetch_add on next_unit) stays a one-liner either way.

critics.notes:
Short version: the PR2' plan is the right shape for Ben (one layout owner, the cache picks both the kernel and the packer, no layout clause in self_attention.hpp) and it preserves PR 4957's bytes, scores and test counts. Three corrections matter: resolve the kernel call inside the merge commit so no commit is red for the dispatch test; add the four stale comments and the PR-body rewrite to the steps; and fix d2 with `Page::layout_t::primary_geometry.head_size` plus a positive control, because `page` has no head_size member.

Words used here: the cache = h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp (struct page); the option = CMake option TRON_K_VNNI; a VNNI slot = K storage of a 128-dimension head in the AMX right-operand layout when the option is on; the kernel = qk_vnni_128x4 (the AMX QK kernel of PR 4957); the packers = pack_q_rows_128x4 (VNNI) and pack_q_group_128x4 (row-major); the reader = k_vnni::qk_group (AVX-512 scoring of a VNNI plane); the dispatch test = t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp (counts packer and kernel calls with fakes); d1/d2/d3 = the three defects of Ben's head listed in design.md section 2; P1-P5 and C1-C16 = the items of ben-profile.md.

verdicts.section: PR3' step 2a: page::k_block_tokens<geometry>() (16 for VNNI, 0 for row-major) replaces the two layout_on gates
verdicts.concern: Three problems. (1) A size whose value 0 means 'no block save' is a sentinel; Ben's C7 (named bool constants are a smell, use an enum) and his P4 pattern (try_score_k_amx returns a run-time 'declined' [kv_cache.hpp:2015-2031 at ade89a9d9c] instead of exposing a compile-time predicate to the caller) show he prefers operations that do the right thing over predicates tested at the call site. (2) It renames the gate but keeps two control flows in store_k_block: the row-major loop [model.hpp:3211-3222 at b39765ec29] and the VNNI run scan [3222-3293]; that is the P3 defect Ben removed from apply_page_tok in e17a12ff09. (3) At his head the page exposes no layout fact; this would be the first, used in two places (k_store_shared at 3154 and store_k_block at 3211).
verdicts.change: Give page::set_k_block a row-major body (for each present lane: kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).k_at(c * 16 + t).set(rows[t]); 4 lines next to Ben's set_k_row(expr) at kv_cache.hpp:2049-2065 of ade89a9d9c). store_k_block then has one flow: run scan, then one set_k_block per (run, kv_head), no layout query. The run granule k_store_block [model.hpp:3139] becomes a plain page constant page::k_block_tokens (= k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16, no geometry parameter, no sentinel). Exactly one layout fact remains, in k_store_shared [3152-3161]: sharing pays only for the VNNI scatter. Expose it as one constexpr bool predicate on page named for the fact (for example page::k_store_is_scatter<geometry>()), with the comment 'the row-major store is 4 line stores per row and stays on main; sharing it was not measured'. Bytes unchanged; the row-major path gains the run scan (a few ns per token, est.); the option-off test's `opened == 0` expectation still holds because sharing stays VNNI-only.

verdicts.section: PR3' step 2c: conversion of non-bf16 rows moves into the cache; the 1-token path calls set_k_row(expr); a new set_k_block overload takes std::array<Row, 16> plus `present`
verdicts.concern: Direction right (Ben moved exactly this dispatch into set_k_row(expr) in ade89a9d9c, model.hpp:3096-3101). Three shape problems. (1) 'A new overload' leaves two public set_k_block signatures (pointer array [kv_cache.hpp:2089-2097 at b39765ec29] and view array): parallel entry points, Ben's C6 (4065141577). (2) `__mmask16 present` stays in a page signature and in model.hpp [3245, 3253]: an x86 intrinsic type at the model layer, which is why model.hpp includes <immintrin.h> [16]. (3) Routing 1-token runs through Ben's expr overload costs a 256-byte stack copy per (token, kv_head) for bf16 rows: a non-const `view` cannot deduce the const_k_row_view overload (different class templates), so the expr overload is chosen and copies before store_row [kv_cache.hpp:2057-2061 at ade89a9d9c], where the PR head reads in place through k_source_row(view) [model.hpp:3266-3268; the overload at k_vnni.hpp:220-225 requires stride 1]. At decode rates this is below measurement (2,304 rows per step at ~15 ns = ~35 us against a ~30 ms step, est.), but it is a regression against the PR head for no gain.
verdicts.change: One page signature: `template <kv_geometry geometry, typename Row> void set_k_block(kv_slot_id slot, size_t kv_head, size_t c, const std::array<Row, k_block_tokens>& rows)`, where an absent lane is a default (invalid) view: `explicit view(T* = nullptr)` and `valid()` exist [view.hpp:116-140]. Inside the cache: derive the lane mask from valid(), use contiguous bf16 views in place (k_source_row(view) overload), convert other scalars into a 16 x 256-byte stack block, and choose store_row for one lane and store_block otherwise, so k_scatter_run_len [model.hpp:3141] moves into the cache that knows its store costs. The raw-pointer store_block stays a tensor operation (t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:241 calls it directly). model.hpp then has no __mmask16, k_source_row, k_destination_row, rows_are_bf16 or conv. PR 4959's set_k_block without `present` [stack/pr4959.diff:465-475] then needs no signature change, only an assertion that all 16 lanes are valid.

verdicts.section: PR3' step 2d: the window protocol becomes operations of batch::k_store_window_t (open / enter / claim / finish / join, watchdog constants as members)
verdicts.concern: The codebase already has this protocol. tron::barrier (Note [Resettable Barrier Design], threading.hpp:873-975) offers reset(n_participants), next_phase(action) (= open: waits for the previous phase, resets the working count, runs the action, releases the phase counter), wait(participant_ix) (= enter: waits for phase >= my completed phase + 1, so a helper's W-th call meets the W-th phase, which is exactly the helper_windows pairing), done(participant_ix) (= finish) and wait_for_all() (= join). It is already a member of batch (free_scratchpads_barrier, common.hpp:1165), is reset per pass in batch::reset_channels(n_attn_workers, n_main_workers) [common.hpp:1071-1074], and is driven the same way from self_attention.hpp:740 (next_phase), 748 and 765 (wait(worker_ix)), 844 (done(worker_ix)). The participant count the window needs is available at that reset: the generated run() calls reset_channels(n_attn_workers, n_workers) with n_workers = 1 + n_main_helpers [ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:1358, 1392] before it launches the helpers [1362-1364]. Its latches wait through the mwaitx readiness source [threading.hpp:125-135 -> h/system/mwaitx.hpp:228], which on Intel is a spin+pause or RTM loop, not a sleep [h/system/mwaitx.hpp:49-58; src/system/mwaitx.cpp:82, 219], the same latency class as the PR's _mm_pause loops [model.hpp:3337, 3354]. A watchdog exists (TRON_LATCH_WATCHDOG, threading.hpp:174-175, 227-240), which answers the PR body's 'join watchdog, reviewers decide' open item. Ben's C4 ('Why not use mask_t?'), C12 (he deduplicated a repeated pattern himself, PR 4697) and his 'spaghetti' remark (P5) predict the question 'why not barrier?'. Wrapping the hand-written counters in member functions keeps a second barrier implementation 300 lines from the first.
verdicts.change: Replace the counters by `barrier k_store_barrier` in batch (constructed like free_scratchpads_barrier at common.hpp:1034, reset with n_main_workers at 1073). Keep only next_unit, unit_start and n_units in a small struct. save_k_impl: main = cut units; k_store_barrier.next_phase([&] { next_unit = 0; }); claim loop; done(0); wait_for_all(). helper = wait(worker_ix); claim loop; done(worker_ix). Delete opened, finished, helper_windows, max_shared_workers (the 128-worker cap goes away), k_join_clock_spins, k_join_timeout_s, the <chrono> and _mm_pause includes: about 45 lines. Costs to state in the plan: the section 4 rule 'memory orders unchanged' no longer holds to the letter (the happens-before comes from the latch's fetch_sub / acquire wait); the test's window checks [t_llama_unit.cpp:4037, 4062, 4078-4093, 4140, 4157] must be rewritten (keep next_unit == n_units + n_workers and the unit invariants; replace the finished_at_return proxy by calling check(before) right after main's save_k returns and before the helper threads are joined, which proves the production join directly); the test must call q_batch.reset_channels(0, n_workers) instead of (0, 0) [t_llama_unit.cpp:~3967] before the three-thread section. If the owner keeps the custom type, the struct comment must say why barrier was not used, and Ben will still ask.

Short version: the PR3' plan reaches 'no layout_on in model.hpp' but not Ben's shape; three remedies invent what the tree already has. Words used here: the cache = h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp (struct page); the PR head = b39765ec29 at /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-split-pr3; Ben's head = ade89a9d9c at /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-pr5047; the window = batch::k_store_window (common.hpp:1196-1219 at the PR head); barrier = tron::barrier, the resettable phase barrier of h/tron/threading.hpp; a run = consecutive minibatch items inside one 16-token block of one page; a lane = one of the 16 token positions of a block.

Evidence base. Merge-tree of origin/bgamari/vnnik-1 into HEAD (merge base a5697f86d3, confirmed by git merge-base) saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-jhan-workspace-intel-AMX-random/e5f1ec3f-7cb5-4755-a5bc-0280de828ba5/scratchpad/mt-4958-critic.txt: 9 conflict hunks at its lines 216, 269, 286 (kv_cache.hpp), 642 (model.hpp), 742, 763, 783 (self_attention.hpp), 827 (tensor/k_vnni.hpp), 1182 (t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp). Facts that decided the verdicts: barrier's reset/next_phase/wait/done/wait_for_all [threading.hpp:897, 915, 930, 936, 926], its use from self_attention.hpp:740/748/765/844, batch::reset_channels at common.hpp:1071-1074 receiving n_main_workers, the generated run() passing n_workers = 1 + n_main_helpers to reset_channels before launching helpers [TronCpp.hs:1358, 1362-1364, 1392], the latch wait being a spin+pause or RTM loop on Intel [h/system/mwaitx.hpp:49-58, 228; src/system/mwaitx.cpp:82, 219], the TRON_LATCH_WATCHDOG watchdog [threading.hpp:174-175, 227-240], view's default constructor and valid() [view.hpp:116-140], the k_source_row(view) overload requiring stride 1 [k_vnni.hpp:220-225], Ben's set_k_row(expr) copying before store_row [kv_cache.hpp:2057-2061 at ade89a9d9c], and PR 4959's get_k_row reading row-major blocks internally [stack/pr4959.diff hunk at kv_cache.hpp:2337-2345].

(2) Inside the page the private mask is enough: `k_vnni_blocks_[k_state_ix(slot)].load(acquire) == k_vnni::BLOCKS_PER_PAGE_MASK_0XF`. verdicts.section: PR4' step 2b: score_k splits live tokens by block layout; one shared dotter helper
verdicts.concern: The split is right and the scores are preserved: each token's score is one dot product, independent of the order of scoring, so moving the tail tokens from PR 4959's in-loop scoring [self_attention.hpp:2008-2017] to after the loop changes no value, and masking keeps the reader's contract (bits of row-major blocks clear) [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:28-32]. Two shape problems. (1) A member helper taking (q, kv_head, live, scores, stride, row accessor) has six parameters. Ben flags long argument lists and placeholder lambdas (C3, P3; the ben-review rule is four parameters). (2) PR 4959 builds the four dotters on every software visit of a VNNI page [self_attention.hpp:1956-1961]. Each dotter converts 128 bf16 query values to fp32 [tron-pr5047 h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp:20-24], so that is 2 KiB of conversion per (page, kv_head) visit even when every live token is in a converted block. Ben's score_k builds them only in the row-major branch. The plan's helper must keep Ben's lazy construction. The plan also leaves one API unnamed: the expansion of the 4-bit block mask to a 64-bit token mask. k_block_bits(c) exists as a private static [kv_cache.hpp:2540]; the expansion does not.
verdicts.change: Inside score_k, define one local generic lambda `score_rows(uint64_t rows, auto row_at)` that captures q, kv_head, scores and stride, builds the dotter array inside, and loops over the bits of `rows`. Row-major branch: `score_rows(live, [&](size_t i) { return keys[i]; })`. VNNI branch: `const uint64_t vnni = live & k_vnni_token_mask(blocks); if (vnni) k_vnni::qk_group(...vnni...); if (live & ~vnni) score_rows(live & ~vnni, [&](size_t i) { return row_major_row(plane, i); });`. Both row types are accepted by dotter::operator() [tron-pr5047 dotter.hpp:27-35]. Add a private `static constexpr uint64_t k_vnni_token_mask(uint8_t blocks)` next to k_block_bits: a loop over the 4 blocks with k_block_bits(c), no multiply trick (C15). Do not make the helper a member function.

verdicts.section: PR4' step 2c: page::k_staging_row and the full.hpp pointer return
verdicts.concern: Ben would reject it. It re-introduces what his second commit removed on purpose: a page operation that hands out a raw bf16* into K storage (P2 "remove the public raw K views"; his Note item 6 "pages expose row transfers and scoring, not K storage views"; C5 "pointers floating around"). It also undoes the symmetry he made with v_head_fn, which always copies into scratch [tron-pr5047 h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2747-2766; kv_cache.hpp Note item 4]. An existing operation covers the need: PR 4959's get_k_row follows the block bit [tron-split-pr4 kv_cache.hpp:2334-2348], so a row of a row-major block is one 4-line read (load_row_major) plus a 256-byte copy into gof::populate's k_scratch, which is L1-resident [src/tron/gof.cpp:201-211]. That is the issue #4500 recovery; the 64-line gather is gone either way. The copy's cost is measured inside the band in every FPGA-attention cell of the 2026-10-21 campaign (head:base, option OFF, 2 repetitions, interim) [/home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/results/pr5047-20261020/results.json]: qwen3-4b tp2 prompt 1024 TPS +0.28 % (band 1.76 TPS), prefill +0.011 s (band 0.15 s); gpt-oss-120b tp4 prompt 1024 TPS -1.66 % (band 6.6 TPS); qwen3-4b tp2 prompt 8192 TPS +0.27 % (1 repetition). The design's section 5 attributes the llama +0.5 % prefill delta to this memcpy. That is wrong: the llama cells ran CPU attention (USE_HW_ATTN=0) [exec/pr5047-20261020/README.md:14, 50-55], where k_head_fn never runs. The step is also a new feature relative to PR3' (section 4 forbids new features), and PR 4959's FPGA numbers (+2.5 % and +12.1 % TPS against the parent) were measured with the pointer path, so they need a re-measurement with or without it.

verdicts.section: PR4' step 2e: tests without raw plane access
verdicts.concern: The direction is right (Ben's P2: tests go through t/kv_cache_helpers.hpp and the page's operations). Two sub-items are wrong as written. (1) t_llama_unit check_page_range_reductions [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2559-2606]: "fill_random -> get_k_row per row -> set_k_row per row" is the identity on an unconverted block. get_k_row reads load_row_major and set_k_row writes store_row_major into the same bytes [kv_cache.hpp:2291-2305, 2334-2348]. So the round trip is dead work. Only the recording loop [:2600-2605] is needed: block_to_vnni transposes whatever bytes fill_random wrote, and the reference copy-out already reads through get_k_row [:2612-2620]. The cross-build "same K instance as the row-major build" property is lost either way; no test compares across builds. (2) t_k_vnni_layout page case [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:616-790]: the raw checks at :662-694 (plane.at for block 0, row_major_row for block 1) are subsumed by the tensor-level case "row-major tail block converts to the VNNI layout and back, bit for bit" [:253-342], which owns its plane and keeps raw access. critics.notes:
Words used here: the cache = h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp (struct page); the kernel = the AMX QK kernel qk_vnni_128x4; the reader = k_vnni::qk_group (AVX-512 scoring of the VNNI plane); the dotter = the per-token AVX-512 dot product over a row-major row; a block = 16 consecutive tokens of a 64-token KV page; a VNNI slot = a K storage slot of a 128-dimension head when the TRON_K_VNNI option is on; the staging = gof::populate copying K and V rows into the FPGA DMA buffer; P1-P5 and C1-C16 = the items of ben-profile.md. Line numbers 'tron-split-pr4' are at PR 4959's head 6b081187e1 in /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-split-pr4; 'tron-pr5047' are at Ben's head ade89a9d9c in /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-pr5047. No file in either worktree was modified.

Short version: the PR4' plan is right in direction (gate and tail scoring inside the cache, self_attention.hpp untouched from PR3'), and two of its steps need to change. Step 2c (k_staging_row, a pointer into the page returned to the staging) should be dropped: it reverses Ben's own removal of raw K views, the existing get_k_row already gives the 4-line read for a row-major block, and the copy it would save measures inside the band in every FPGA cell of the 2026-10-21 campaign. Step 2e's test recipe has one no-op sub-item (a get_k_row/set_k_row round trip on an unconverted block is the identity) and one sub-item that no page operation can express (bytes of a block whose bit was dropped).

Method: read ben-profile.md, design.md, pr4959.diff (2334 lines), pr4959-body.md, ben-corpus.md, pr5047-c1.diff, pr5047-c2.diff; ran the merge-tree simulation (13 conflict hunks, saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-jhan-workspace-intel-AMX-random/e5f1ec3f-7cb5-4755-a5bc-0280de828ba5/scratchpad/critic-pr4-merge-tree.txt) and read every hunk; located each symbol in both trees; read the campaign README and results.json for the FPGA cells. critics.notes:
Short version. The four lenses and the brief cover Ben's P1-P5 and C5/C6/C13 well, but seven kinds of objection in his record are not covered: names (C1), comment volume (C9), function surgery in the cache's copy and forget paths (C3), duplicated layout state plus a growing vector in model.hpp (P1, C13), a hand-rolled join beside the existing latch (C4, C6), dead per-batch state in builds that never share (C11), and a repeated test pattern (C12).
